title: Cold War crises
examples: How did the Cold War affect everyday life in different countries?
What were the main differences between the goals of the US and the USSR?
Why did the superpowers keep fighting without direct war?

explain.say: Today we study the Cold War crises. These were times of high tension between the US and the USSR. We will look at four key moments. These moments shaped the world for decades.

draw.text: Cold War Crises: Berlin, Korea, Cuba, Vietnam

explain.say: First we look at the Berlin Blockade. The Soviet Union blocked all roads to West Berlin. The Western Allies responded with an airlift to keep people supplied. This showed early superpower tension.

draw.text: Berlin Blockade: Airlift supplies West Berlin

explain.say: Next is the Korean War. The conflict was a proxy war fought between North and South Korea. The US supported the South while China supported the North. It showed the Cold War spreading to Asia.

draw.text: Korean War: North vs South Korea

explain.say: Then we examine the Cuban Missile Crisis. The USSR placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, near the US. This brought the world closer to nuclear war than ever before. It was a very tense standoff.

draw.text: Cuban Missile Crisis: Missiles in Cuba

explain.say: Finally, we look at the Vietnam War. This was a long conflict involving the US and communist forces. It highlighted the difficulty of containing communism globally. The US eventually withdrew its forces.

draw.text: Vietnam War: US withdrawal of forces

explain.say: In everyday life, these crises show us how global politics affects local decisions. For example, trade routes might be closed due to political tension. This affects the cost of goods for everyone.

faq.q: Why was the Cuban Missile Crisis so dangerous?
faq.a: It was dangerous because nuclear missiles were placed so close to the United States. It made the world feel like it was minutes away from nuclear war.
asks: What was the biggest danger of the Cold War?
How close did the world come to nuclear war?

faq.q: What was the main difference between the Berlin and Korean crises?
faq.a: The Berlin crisis focused on controlling a single city. The Korean crisis involved two entire nations fighting for control.
asks: Were the crises about cities or countries?
How did the scale of the conflict differ?

faq.q: Was the Vietnam War purely about communism?
faq.a: While communism was a major factor, the war also involved national identity and self-determination for the Vietnamese people. It was complex.
asks: Was it just a communist fight?
What were the other reasons for the fighting?

faq.q: What does 'proxy war' mean in this context?
faq.a: A proxy war means that the superpowers fought indirectly by supporting smaller local groups. They avoided direct fighting with each other.
asks: Did the US and USSR fight directly?
What is the term for fighting through others?

faq.q: Did the Cold War end suddenly?
faq.a: No, the end was a process involving changes in leadership and economic conditions in the Soviet Union. It was gradual rather than a single event.
asks: When did the Cold War actually finish?
What caused the end of the superpower rivalry?

facts: The Cold War was a period of political tension between the US and the USSR.
The Berlin Airlift successfully supplied West Berlin after the Soviet blockade.
The Cuban Missile Crisis involved the discovery of Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba.
The Korean War was an early example of a proxy conflict.

quiz.say: The Soviet Union blocked access to West Berlin by controlling all roads. This action was known as the:
quiz.why: The blockade was the specific action taken by the Soviets to cut off supplies.

wrong.0: This term relates to Cuba, not the city of Berlin.
wrong.1: This describes a type of conflict, not the specific action in Berlin.
wrong.3: The airlift was the response to the blockade, not the blockade itself.

quiz.say: The placement of nuclear missiles in Cuba caused which crisis?
quiz.why: The missiles in Cuba were the direct cause of this specific, high-stakes confrontation.

wrong.0: Vietnam was a long war of national struggle, not a sudden missile deployment.
wrong.2: The Berlin crisis involved land and air access, not nuclear weapons.
wrong.3: The Korean War was a conflict between two nations, not a missile placement.

quiz.say: In the Korean War, the US generally supported which side?
quiz.why: The US military intervention was primarily aimed at supporting the established government in South Korea.

wrong.1: North Korea was supported by the Soviet Union and China at the time.
wrong.2: China supported the North Korean side during this conflict.
wrong.3: While the people were involved, the US supported the recognized government structure.
